text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat hold talks on the Middle East peace process. Arafat says that the Palestinians are facing difficulties in their talks with Israel on implementing the peace accords, but that there was still hope to arrive at a solution which would be satisfactory to the Palestinian people.
The talks between Mubarak and Arafat follow a letter the Egyptian president sent to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
- Egyptian cabinet to discuss new laws on Wednesday designed to facilitate investment.
- Egypt refuses to sell cement company to the Israeli conglomerate Koor, according to a report in an Israeli newspaper.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa goes to Lisbon to attend the European security meeting.
- Egypt's health minister Ismail Sallam says that Egypt intends to wipe out children's polio by the year 2000.
